key_findings.value: No carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after a heat treatment of 14 days at 320 °C.

source.reason: Metallographic inspection (after nitric-acid etching) is the technique used to reveal precipitates/carbides, and is the method by which the absence of carbides in this sample was established.

key_findings.value: The rare globular inclusions (up to 30 µm diameter) in the monocrystals were identified as AlN by EDX analysis.

source.reason: The experimental section describes SEM/EDX used for qualitative precipitate analysis; the AlN inclusions in the monocrystals were identified by EDX.

duration.value: about 12 h (crystal growth with subsequent cooling)

processing_steps_notes.value: Monocrystals with up to 10 cm length were grown by the Bridgman method (10–15 mm/h pulling rate); the crystal growth with subsequent cooling occurred within a time period of about 12 h. The Fe-16%Al monocrystal (nominal 16 at.% Al, real 16.0 at.%) is one of these monocrystals.

source.reason: The studied sample is a monocrystal; the experimental section describes how the monocrystals were produced (Bridgman growth), establishing the sample's fabrication history.

processing_steps_notes.value: The Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C was heat-treated for 14 days at 320 °C; no carbides were detected after this treatment. Per the experimental section, all heat treatments other than the short (<300 °C) ones were performed with the specimens enclosed in evacuated (10^-6 bar) SiO2 capsules.

source.reason: The process defining this sample is a 14-day 320 °C heat treatment applied to the Fe-16%Al monocrystal (45 ppm C); the general experimental section specifies the encapsulating atmosphere for heat treatments above 300 °C.

aliases.value: Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after 14 days at 320 °C

source.reason: The Fe-16%Al monocrystal is a single-phase Fe-Al solid solution; the matrix phase is inferred as the solid solution in which inclusions were found.
The monocrystals (including the Fe-16%Al monocrystal) contained rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm, identified by EDX.
The sample is a monocrystal with rare globular AlN inclusions and, after 14 days at 320 °C, no detectable carbides.

overall_structure.value: Fe-16%Al monocrystal (45 ppm C) after 14 days at 320 °C: single-phase bcc Fe-Al solid solution (monocrystal, no grain boundaries) containing rare globular AlN inclusions up to 30 µm. No carbides were detected after this heat treatment (unlike polycrystals and the Fe-17%Al monocrystal).

source.reason: Microstructural description of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal (45 ppm C): AlN inclusions present in monocrystals, and no carbides detected after the 14-day 320 °C heat treatment that defines this sample.

unmapped_findings: Sample composition (Table 1, monocrystal nominal 16 at.% Al): real Al 16.0 at.% (8.4 wt.-%), C 45 wt.ppm, Si 40 wt.ppm, O 60 wt.ppm; the Fe-16%Al monocrystal is (111)-oriented and is one of the monocrystals containing rare globular AlN inclusions up to 30 µm.

The Fe-16%Al monocrystal was studied by microhardness (Fig. 1) and compressive stress-strain (Fig. 2) as a function of prior heat treatment, but no hardness or yield-stress value is reported for the 320 °C/14 d condition specifically; the hardness plot (Fig. 1) lists 320 °C/233 d (a different duration) and 300 °C/14 d instead, so no mechanical property value can be attributed to this 320 °C/14 d sample.

Without heat treatment no carbides were found in all monocrystals, and heat treatment at 320 °C for 14 days produced less carbides without loading (carbides detected in the Fe-17%Al monocrystal with 70 ppm C only when loaded concurrently at 100 MPa).
